images.caption: Home in Falcon Heights, Minnesota, between Snelling and Hamline Avenues, and between Larpenteur and Roselawn Avenues.

place.source_title: Home in Falcon Heights (Residential architecture of Falcon Heights, Minnesota 01)

brief: Post-war one-storey brick rambler in a St. Paul suburb: a low hipped-and-gabled asphalt roof with a massive brick chimney, tan-brown brick walls, a corner picture window and a front bay, a small entrance stoop and an attached garage wing, a flowering tree and a sweep of lawn.

facade.notes: a 1952 buff-brick ranch in Falcon Heights MN: a front-gabled entry bay with a round window, picture windows with striped aluminium awnings, a big end chimney, foundation shrubs; a walk to the sidewalk; an ornamental tree flaring red in autumn; campaign lawn signs

why.note: the early-1950s brick ranch of the Twin Cities' first-ring suburbs
aluminium awnings over the south windows: pre-air-conditioning shade
